items.question: How is the R22 main rotor hub attached to the mast, and how are the blades attached to the hub?
options: Blades mounted to the hub by coning hinges; the hub mounted to the shaft by a teeter hinge
items.explanation: The main rotor has two all-metal blades mounted to the hub by coning hinges; the hub is mounted to the shaft by a teeter hinge. Coning and teeter hinges use self-lubricated bearings.

items.question: What is the function of the main rotor droop stops?
options: To provide a teeter-hinge friction restraint that normally prevents teetering while stopping or starting
To lock the blades for transport
items.explanation: Droop stops provide a teeter-hinge friction restraint which normally prevents the rotor from teetering while stopping or starting.

items.question: Why must an R22 main rotor blade be refinished if the paint erodes to bare metal at the skin-to-spar bond line?
options: The bond may be damaged if the bond line is exposed
items.explanation: Each blade has a thick stainless steel leading-edge spar; the skins are bonded to it about one inch aft of the leading edge. Blades must be refinished if paint erodes to bare metal at the skin-to-spar bond line — the bond may be damaged if the bond line is exposed.

items.question: How is engine power transmitted to the upper drive sheave?
options: Vee-belts from a sheave bolted directly to the engine output shaft
A driveshaft with a fluid coupling
items.explanation: A vee-belt sheave is bolted directly to the engine output shaft; vee-belts transmit power to the upper sheave, which contains an overrunning clutch in its hub.

items.question: Where is the overrunning (sprag) clutch located in the R22 drive system?
options: In the hub of the upper drive sheave
items.explanation: The upper sheave has an overrunning clutch contained in its hub; the inner shaft of the clutch transmits power forward to the main rotor and aft to the tail rotor, allowing the rotor to keep turning in autorotation.

items.question: How is the R22 main gearbox lubricated and mounted?
options: Splash lubricated, supported by four rubber mounts
Dry sump with an external pump
items.explanation: The main gearbox contains a single-stage spiral-bevel gear set which is splash lubricated, and it is supported by four rubber mounts. A cooling duct under the box connects to the top of the engine shroud.

items.question: What kind of engine powers the R22?
options: A Lycoming four-cylinder, horizontally-opposed, air-cooled, carbureted engine with a wet-sump oil system
items.explanation: One Lycoming four-cylinder, horizontally-opposed, overhead-valve, air-cooled, carbureted engine with a wet-sump oil system powers the helicopter; it has a starter, alternator, shielded ignition, two magnetos, muffler, oil cooler and induction air filter.

items.question: How is cooling air supplied to the R22 cylinders and oil cooler?
options: A direct-drive squirrel-cage fan on the engine output shaft feeding a fiberglass/aluminum shroud
items.explanation: A direct-drive, squirrel-cage fan mounted to the engine output shaft supplies cooling air to the cylinders and oil cooler via a fiberglass and aluminum shroud.

items.question: How does the pilot select cool or heated induction air on the R22?
options: A pilot-controlled sliding valve in the carburetor air box that admits either cool or warm (hot-scoop) air
There is no carb heat on the R22
items.explanation: Induction air enters through a right-side inlet and passes to the carburetor air box; a hot-air scoop supplies heated air, and a sliding valve controlled by the pilot allows either cool or warm air into the box, through the filter and up into the carburetor.

items.question: How are the R22 primary flight controls actuated?
items.explanation: All primary controls are actuated through push-pull tubes and bellcranks. Bearings are sealed ball bearings or self-lubricated liners. There is no hydraulic boost.

items.question: How is the engine throttle linked to the collective?
options: By a mechanical correlation linkage — raising the collective opens the throttle, lowering it closes the throttle
items.explanation: The engine throttle is correlated to collective inputs through a mechanical linkage: raising the collective opens the throttle, lowering it closes the throttle. The collective also carries a twist-grip throttle.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: FLIGHT CONTROLS / ENGINE CONTROLS (p.7-4, 7-8)

items.question: Above what altitude do the throttle-collective correlation and governor become less effective, requiring slow, smooth power changes?
items.explanation: A caution notes that above 4000 feet, throttle-collective correlation and the governor are less effective; power changes should be slow and smooth, and RPM must often be controlled with collective as the throttle is frequently wide open.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: FLIGHT CONTROLS (p.7-4); Sec 10 Safety Tip 13

items.question: The RPM governor is active only above what engine RPM?
items.explanation: The governor senses RPM changes and applies corrective throttle through a friction clutch that the pilot can easily override. It is active only above 80% engine RPM and is switched with a toggle on the end of the right-seat collective.

items.question: What is a limitation of the RPM governor noted in Section 7?
options: It may not prevent over- or under-speed conditions generated by aggressive flight maneuvers
It disables itself in a turn
It requires the battery switch off
items.explanation: The governor is designed to assist in controlling RPM under normal conditions; it may not prevent over- or under-speed conditions generated by aggressive flight maneuvers, and at high density altitude its response rate may be too slow to prevent overspeed during gusts, pull-ups or when lowering collective.

items.question: What is the purpose of the collective-up trim spring?
options: To hold the collective down in autorotation
To balance the rotor loads so the pilot can remove the left hand from the collective in most flight regimes
items.explanation: Balancing trim springs are in the cyclic and collective controls. The collective-up spring balances the rotor loads, allowing the pilot to remove the left hand from the collective during most flight regimes.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: CONTROL TRIM AND FRICTION (p.7-7)

items.question: What does the longitudinal cyclic bungee spring do?
options: Provides an on-off trim like the lateral spring
It is a fixed bungee that cancels most longitudinal stick forces during cruise flight
It adds friction to the collective
items.explanation: The longitudinal cyclic has a fixed bungee spring which cancels most longitudinal stick forces during cruise flight. The lateral cyclic has an on-off trim spring for the high-speed left stick force.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: CONTROL TRIM AND FRICTION (p.7-7)

items.question: Why should the pilot reach around the LEFT side of the cyclic center post to actuate the lateral trim?
options: To avoid inadvertently pulling the mixture control, which would cause engine stoppage
To avoid the carb heat control
To keep the right hand on the collective
items.explanation: A caution: if the mixture control is inadvertently pulled in flight, engine stoppage will result. To avoid pulling the wrong control, always reach around the left side of the cyclic center post to actuate the lateral trim.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: CONTROL TRIM AND FRICTION (p.7-7); Safety Notice SN-1

items.question: Do the R22 tail rotor pedals have any trim spring or friction device?
options: No — the pedals actuate push-pull controls directly to the tail rotor pitch control with no trim spring or friction
items.explanation: The pedals actuate push-pull controls connected directly to the tail rotor pitch control and do not incorporate any trim spring or friction devices.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: CONTROL TRIM AND FRICTION (p.7-7)

items.question: What is the purpose of the throttle overtravel spring?
options: To let the pilot roll the throttle off beyond the idle stop before a run-on autorotation landing, preventing the throttle opening as collective is raised
To bias the governor toward higher RPM
To hold the twist grip at cruise setting
items.explanation: An overtravel spring in the throttle linkage lets the pilot roll the throttle off beyond the idle stop prior to a ground-contact (run-on) autorotation landing, preventing the throttle from opening when collective is raised. Correct adjustment can be checked in preflight.

items.question: How is correct throttle linkage adjustment verified during preflight?
options: Roll the twist-grip through the overtravel spring and hold against the hard idle stop; the carburetor throttle arm should just barely start to move when the collective is raised full up
items.explanation: Roll the twist-grip through the overtravel spring and hold it against the hard idle stop. The carburetor throttle arm should just barely start to move when the collective is raised full up.

items.question: How does the clutch actuator tension the drive belts, and when does it switch off?
options: It applies a fixed time of travel
An electric actuator raises the upper sheave; it senses compressive load (belt tension) and switches off when the belts are properly tensioned
It runs until the pilot releases the switch
items.explanation: After start, an electric actuator between the drive sheaves raises the upper sheave when the clutch switch is engaged. It senses compressive load (belt tension) and switches off when the vee-belts are properly tensioned; the clutch caution light is on whenever the circuit is energized.

items.question: If the clutch actuator fuse blows, what happens?
options: The circuit breaker trips and the light goes out
The actuator motor stops but the clutch caution light remains illuminated
items.explanation: A fuse on or near the test-switch panel prevents an actuator overload from tripping the breaker. If the fuse blows, the actuator motor stops but the clutch caution light remains illuminated. An open circuit breaker removes power from both the motor and the light.

items.question: How does fuel reach the engine in the R22?
options: Gravity flow — there are no fuel pumps
items.explanation: The fuel system is gravity-flow (no fuel pumps) and includes a main tank, an optional auxiliary tank, a shutoff valve behind the left seat, and a strainer (gascolator).

items.question: Why does the R22 auxiliary fuel tank empty before the main tank?
options: It is interconnected with the main tank and mounted somewhat higher, so it empties first while fuel still remains in the main tank
A valve draws from it first
items.explanation: The auxiliary tank is interconnected with the main tank and located somewhat higher, so it becomes empty first while fuel still remains in the main tank. The fuel shutoff valve controls flow from both tanks.

items.question: How many fuel sampling locations should be drained before the first flight of the day, and where does the low fuel light get its signal?
options: One location; the light shares the main gage float
All three drain locations (both tank sumps and the gascolator); the low fuel light has a separate electric sender on the bottom of the main tank
Two locations; the light is mechanical
None required; the gages are sufficient
items.explanation: Fuel should be sampled from all three locations (gascolator and each tank sump) before the first flight and after refueling. The low fuel caution light is actuated by a separate electric sender on the bottom of the main tank, independent of the gages.

items.question: What voltage is the R22 electrical system?
options: 14-volt DC with an alternator and a sealed lead-acid battery
items.explanation: A 14-volt DC electrical system including an alternator and a sealed lead-acid battery is standard. The battery is in the engine compartment or beneath the instrument console.

items.question: What continues to receive power with the battery switch off, and how?
options: The tachometers and the clock, via a fused wire that bypasses the battery relay
The landing lights, via a capacitor
items.explanation: The battery switch controls the battery relay. A fused wire near the battery bypasses the relay so both tachometers and the clock continue to receive battery power with the battery switch off.

items.question: Except for emergency procedures, why should the alternator not be operated with the battery switched off?
options: The battery helps protect electrical equipment from voltage spikes
items.explanation: A note: except for emergency procedures, do not operate the alternator with the battery switched off — the battery helps protect electrical equipment from voltage spikes.

items.question: Is in-flight reset of R22 circuit breakers recommended?
options: No — in-flight reset of circuit breakers is not recommended
items.explanation: The circuit breaker panel is on the ledge forward of the left seat; breakers are marked for function and amperage. In-flight reset of circuit breakers is not recommended.

items.question: Under what condition do the R22 landing lights operate?
options: Whenever the battery switch is on
Only when the clutch actuator switch is in the engage position
Only with the avionics master on
items.explanation: A note in the LIGHTING SYSTEM description: landing lights operate only when the clutch actuator switch is in the engage position. Two landing lights are set at different vertical angles.

items.question: How do the R22 main and tail gearbox chip detectors work?
options: They are magnetic devices in the gearbox drain plugs — metallic particles bridge the magnets and close a circuit to light the caution light
items.explanation: The main and tail gearbox chip detectors are magnetic devices in the drain plug of each gearbox. When metallic particles are drawn to the magnets, they close an electrical circuit, illuminating the caution light — warning of possible impending gearbox failure.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: WARNING AND CAUTION LIGHTS (p.7-24)

items.question: At what rotor RPM does the low-RPM horn sound, and when is it muted?
options: Below 97%; muted when the collective is fully down
items.explanation: All R22s have a low-RPM horn that sounds when rotor RPM is below 97% and is muted when the collective is fully down. On earlier aircraft it comes from a console speaker; on later aircraft, a tone generator provides it through the headsets.

items.question: What does the R22 Engine Monitoring Unit (EMU) do?
options: It is a digital recording device in the governor control box that continuously monitors engine and rotor speed, oil temp, CHT, MAP, ambient pressure and OAT
items.explanation: The EMU, on later aircraft, is a digital recording device within the engine RPM governor control box. It continuously monitors engine and rotor speed, engine oil temperature, cylinder head temperature, manifold pressure, ambient pressure and outside air temperature. It is a maintenance aid only.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: ENGINE MONITORING UNIT (p.7-25)

items.question: What does a FAST flashing EMU status light (about four times per second) indicate?
options: A fault in the EMU senders or circuitry
The EMU has detected an exceedance
items.explanation: Steady light = normal. A slow flash (once per 2 seconds) or no light = a fault in the EMU senders or circuitry. A fast flash (four times per second) = the EMU has detected an exceedance. Faults or exceedances must be investigated and reset by a mechanic before the next flight.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: ENGINE MONITORING UNIT (p.7-25)

items.question: How long does the EMU take to complete its self-test after the battery is switched on?
items.explanation: The EMU requires approximately ten seconds to complete a self-test after the aircraft battery is switched on; once complete, steady illumination means normal operation.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: ENGINE MONITORING UNIT (p.7-25)

items.question: When is the R22 carbon monoxide (CO) detector installed?
options: Only if the optional cabin heater is installed
Only on aircraft used for training
Only on later Beta II aircraft
items.explanation: The CO detector is installed if the optional cabin heater is installed. It consists of a sensor above the pilot's heater outlet and a caution light; a system check (light flashes twice) runs each time power is switched on.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR (p.7-29)

items.question: In case of an in-flight engine fire, why is the heater control knob pushed off?
options: To seal the cabin area from the engine compartment
items.explanation: A caution in CABIN HEATING AND VENTILATION: in case of an in-flight engine fire, the heater control knob should be pushed off to seal the cabin area from the engine compartment.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: CABIN HEATING AND VENTILATION (p.7-26)

items.question: When does skid landing gear crosstube yielding require crosstube replacement?
options: When yielding allows the tail skid to be within 34 inches (24 inches for Standard or HP) of the ground with the helicopter empty on level pavement
When the skid shoes wear through
items.explanation: Most hard landings are absorbed elastically; in an extremely hard landing the struts hinge up and outward as the crosstube yields. Slight yielding is acceptable, but yielding that allows the tail skid to be within 34 inches (24 inches for R22 Standard or HP) of the ground when empty on level pavement requires crosstube replacement.

items.question: When should skid wear shoes be replaced?
options: When the thinnest point in the wear area is less than 0.05 inches (1.3 mm)
items.explanation: Abrasion-resistant wear shoes on the bottom of the skids should be inspected periodically (especially after autorotation landings) and replaced whenever the thinnest point in the wear area is less than 0.05 inches (1.3 mm).

items.question: What two conditions could damage the rotor brake shoes?
options: Applying it above 20% RPM, or holding it for over a minute
Applying it without waiting at least 30 seconds after the engine stops, or using a force that stops the rotor in less than 20 seconds
Using it as a parking brake, or applying it below 10 lb force
Applying it before shutdown, or in cold weather
items.explanation: A caution: applying the rotor brake without waiting at least 30 seconds after the engine stops, or using a force that stops the rotor in less than 20 seconds, may damage the brake shoes. The brake must be released before starting the engine; the starter is disabled when the brake is engaged.

items.question: What is the purpose of the optional engine primer system?
options: To lean the mixture at altitude
To bleed air from the fuel lines
items.explanation: The optional primer improves engine cold starting. The pump is in front of the right seat near the hourmeter; normally two to three strokes are used, pulling the handle up slowly, then pushing it full down and locking after priming.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: ENGINE PRIMER SYSTEM (OPTIONAL) (p.7-28)

items.question: Where is the R22 static source located?
options: Inside the aft cowling, inboard of the cowl door hinge
On the belly near the gascolator
items.explanation: The pitot tube is on the front edge of the mast fairing; the static source is inside the aft cowling, inboard of the cowl door hinge. Water can be drained via plastic plugs accessible through the underside inspection panel if the ASI or altimeter is erratic.

items.question: Why should the helicopter not be stowed with the clutch switch engaged?
options: The tachometers stay powered with the clutch engaged and will discharge the battery
items.explanation: A note under DUAL TACHOMETER: do not stow the helicopter with the clutch switch engaged — the tachometers are powered with the clutch engaged and will discharge the battery.

items.question: What is the total weight limit for items attached to each accessory mounting bar?
items.explanation: There is a 10 lb total weight limit for items attached to each accessory mounting bar; USB and cigarette-lighter-style power outlets protected by the Aux Power breaker are provided near the inboard ends.

items.question: For flight, in what position should the ELT transmitter switch and the cockpit remote switch be set?
options: AUTO / ARM (the remote in its middle position)
items.explanation: The transmitter switch is secured in AUTO/ARM at installation and should always be there for flight; the remote switch/annunciator should also be in the AUTO/ARMED (middle) position. With both in AUTO/ARM, the ELT transmits on a high-G load. Use ON if an emergency landing is imminent and time permits; use RESET to stop an inadvertent activation.
references: R22 POH Sec 7: EMERGENCY LOCATOR TRANSMITTER (OPTIONAL) (p.7-31)
